# mcpwatchman

> Independent, continuous security and quality audit of the servers listed in
> the official Model Context Protocol registry. Free, MIT-licensed, and not
> affiliated with Anthropic or the registry.

## What it does

Scans each registry server's published source and publishes an evidence-linked
assessment. A score opens at 100 and every deduction names the finding, the file
and the line that produced it. Five axes are scored 0-100 independently: Code
Safety (weight 30), Auth Posture (20), Dependency Health (20), Maintenance (15),
Transparency (15).

## Current status

Pre-v0.1. **No scores are published yet.** The scoring engine and the registry
crawler are built and tested; the scanner that feeds them is not. Nothing on
this site should be read as an assessment of any server.

## Stated limits

- The analysis is static. Published source, manifests and lockfiles are read;
  the code is never executed and no running server is ever contacted.
- Coverage is partial and the figure is published: in a 100-server registry
  sample taken 2026-09-14, 50 of 99 active servers shipped a source we can
  fetch. 48 were remote-only with no published source at all.
- The weighted composite score is computed but deliberately not published until
  a hand-audited gold set validates the weights.
